This popular Korean street food offers an irresistible balance of flavors and textures, making it a truly addictive meal. Perfect for sharing, it brings the vibrant taste of Korea right to your home.

instructions.title: Prepare the Chicken
instructions.text: Pat the chicken pieces very dry with paper towels. Season them evenly with salt, black pepper, and ginger powder. In a large bowl, whisk together the all-purpose flour, cornstarch, and baking powder. Gradually add the cold water, mixing until you have a smooth, thin batter. Add the seasoned chicken to the batter, ensuring each piece is fully coated.

instructions.title: First Fry the Chicken
instructions.text: Heat vegetable oil in a large pot or deep fryer to 350F (175C). Carefully add chicken pieces, without overcrowding the pot, and fry for 6-8 minutes until light golden brown and cooked through. Remove the chicken and place it on a wire rack set over a baking sheet to drain. Repeat with remaining chicken.

instructions.title: Prepare the Yangnyeom Sauce
instructions.text: While the chicken is frying, prepare the sauce. In a medium saucepan, combine gochujang, soy sauce, rice vinegar, honey or corn syrup, brown sugar, minced garlic, minced ginger, sesame oil, and 2 tablespoons of water. Bring the mixture to a gentle simmer over medium heat, stirring constantly, until the sauce thickens slightly and becomes glossy, about 3-5 minutes. Remove from heat.

instructions.title: Second Fry for Extra Crispiness
instructions.text: Increase the oil temperature to 375F (190C). Return the partially fried chicken to the hot oil in batches. Fry for another 2-3 minutes, or until the chicken is deep golden brown and exceptionally crispy. This double-frying technique is key for authentic Korean fried chicken crispiness. Remove and place on a wire rack.

instructions.title: Coat the Chicken with Sauce
instructions.text: Once all the chicken is double-fried, transfer the hot, crispy chicken directly into the saucepan with the prepared Yangnyeom sauce. Toss gently but quickly to ensure every piece is evenly coated with the delicious, sticky sauce. Work efficiently to maintain the chicken's crispiness.

instructions.title: Garnish and Serve
instructions.text: Transfer the coated Yangnyeom chicken to a serving platter. Garnish generously with toasted sesame seeds and chopped green onions. Serve immediately while hot and crispy. This dish pairs wonderfully with a side of pickled radishes or a simple beer.

tips: For the crispiest chicken, ensure your oil temperature is consistently maintained. A kitchen thermometer is highly recommended for accurate frying.
Adjust the spice level of your Yangnyeom sauce by increasing or decreasing the amount of gochujang. For extra heat, add a pinch of gochugaru Korean chili flakes.
Yangnyeom chicken is best enjoyed fresh. If you have leftovers, reheat in an air fryer or oven to regain some crispiness, though it may not be as crunchy as freshly made.
article:
Mastering Yangnyeom Korean Fried Chicken: Your Ultimate Guide to Authentic Korean Chicken Recipes

There’s something undeniably magical about Korean Fried Chicken. It’s not just fried chicken; it’s an experience. Among the many beloved Korean Chicken Recipes, Yangnyeom Korean Fried Chicken stands out as a global favorite, renowned for its irresistible sticky, sweet, spicy, and savory sauce that coats every perfectly crispy piece of chicken. If you’ve ever dreamed of recreating that authentic Korean restaurant flavor at home, you’re in the right place. This comprehensive guide will walk you through everything you need to know to make the most delicious Yangnyeom Korean Fried Chicken, from achieving that signature double-fried crunch to simmering the perfect glossy sauce.

## What is Yangnyeom Korean Fried Chicken?

Yangnyeom (양념) literally translates to "seasoned sauce," and in the context of fried chicken, it refers to the iconic sweet and spicy glaze that defines this dish. Unlike American fried chicken, which is often served plain or with gravy, Korean fried chicken is famous for its ultra-crispy, thin crust and its variety of flavorful coatings. Yangnyeom Korean Fried Chicken typically features a vibrant red-orange sauce made primarily from gochujang (Korean chili paste), garlic, soy sauce, rice vinegar, and a sweetener like honey or corn syrup.

The secret to its incredible texture lies in the double-frying method. This technique ensures that the chicken skin and batter become incredibly crispy and stay that way, even after being tossed in the thick, luscious sauce. The result is a harmonious blend of textures and flavors: a satisfying crunch followed by juicy, tender chicken enveloped in a complex sauce that's addictively sweet, spicy, tangy, and savory all at once. It’s no wonder this particular Korean Chicken Recipe has captured hearts worldwide.

## Ingredients You Need for Authentic Yangnyeom Chicken

To create the perfect Yangnyeom Korean Fried Chicken, quality ingredients are key. Here’s a breakdown of what you’ll need:

**For the Chicken and Marinade:**
*   **Chicken:** 2-3 lbs chicken wings or boneless, skinless chicken thighs (cut into bite-sized pieces). Wings are traditional, but thighs are great for a meatier bite.
*   **Marinade:**
    *   1 tbsp soy sauce
    *   1 tsp grated fresh ginger
    *   1 tsp minced garlic
    *   1/2 tsp salt
    *   1/4 tsp black pepper
    *   1 tbsp mirin (optional, for tenderness and flavor)

**For the Crispy Batter:**
*   1 cup potato starch or cornstarch (potato starch is preferred for superior crispiness)
*   1/2 cup all-purpose flour
*   1 tsp baking powder (helps with lightness and crispiness)
*   1 large egg
*   1/2 cup cold water (adjust as needed for a thin, pancake-like batter)
*   Pinch of salt
*   **Frying Oil:** 6-8 cups neutral oil with a high smoke point (e.g., canola, vegetable, peanut oil)

**For the Yangnyeom Sauce:**
*   1/4 cup gochujang (Korean chili paste – essential for flavor and color)
*   2 tbsp soy sauce
*   2 tbsp rice vinegar
*   2 tbsp honey or corn syrup (for sweetness and gloss)
*   1 tbsp brown sugar (optional, for extra sweetness and depth)
*   1 tbsp minced garlic
*   1 tsp grated fresh ginger
*   1 tsp gochugaru (Korean chili flakes – adjust for desired heat)
*   1 tsp sesame oil
*   2 tbsp ketchup (adds tanginess and a richer color)
*   1/4 cup water or chicken broth

## Step-by-Step Instructions to Make Crispy Yangnyeom Chicken

Making the perfect Yangnyeom Korean Fried Chicken involves a few distinct stages, but each step is crucial for that authentic taste and texture.

**1. Prepare and Marinate the Chicken:**
   *   Pat the chicken pieces thoroughly dry with paper towels. This removes excess moisture, which is vital for a crispy crust.
   *   In a bowl, combine the chicken with soy sauce, ginger, garlic, salt, pepper, and mirin (if using). Mix well and let it marinate for at least 30 minutes at room temperature, or up to 2 hours in the refrigerator.

**2. Prepare the Batter:**
   *   In a large bowl, whisk together the potato starch, all-purpose flour, baking powder, and salt.
   *   In a separate small bowl, whisk the egg and cold water.
   *   Pour the wet ingredients into the dry ingredients and mix until just combined. A few lumps are okay; overmixing can develop gluten, making the batter tough. The consistency should be like a thin pancake batter.

**3. First Fry (for internal cooking and initial crisping):**
   *   Heat 3-4 inches of frying oil in a large pot or Dutch oven to 325°F (160°C). Use a thermometer for accuracy.
   *   Dip each piece of marinated chicken into the batter, ensuring it’s evenly coated but not too thick.
   *   Carefully lower the chicken pieces into the hot oil, frying in batches to avoid overcrowding. Overcrowding lowers the oil temperature and results in soggy chicken.
   *   Fry for 6-8 minutes, or until the chicken is cooked through and lightly golden brown.
   *   Remove the chicken with a spider or slotted spoon and place it on a wire rack set over a baking sheet to drain. Let it rest for at least 10-15 minutes. This cooling period is essential for the double-fry technique.

**4. Second Fry (for ultimate crispiness):**
   *   Increase the oil temperature to 350-375°F (175-190°C).
   *   Return the chicken to the hot oil in batches.
   *   Fry for another 3-5 minutes, or until the chicken is deep golden brown and exceptionally crispy.
   *   Remove the chicken and place it back on the wire rack to drain any excess oil.

**5. Make the Yangnyeom Sauce:**
   *   While the chicken is resting after its first fry, prepare the sauce. In a medium saucepan, combine all the Yangnyeom sauce ingredients (gochujang, soy sauce, rice vinegar, honey/corn syrup, brown sugar, minced garlic, grated ginger, gochugaru, sesame oil, ketchup, and water/broth).
   *   Bring the mixture to a simmer over medium heat, stirring constantly until it thickens slightly and becomes glossy, about 5-7 minutes. Remove from heat.

**6. Coat the Chicken and Serve:**
   *   Once the chicken has finished its second fry and is still hot, transfer it to a large bowl.
   *   Pour the warm Yangnyeom sauce over the chicken.
   *   Toss gently but quickly with tongs until every piece is evenly coated in the sticky, beautiful sauce.
   *   Serve immediately!

## Pro Tips for the Best Korean Fried Chicken

Achieving that perfect Korean Fried Chicken often comes down to a few key techniques:

*   **Double Frying is Non-Negotiable:** This is the absolute secret to the signature ultra-crispy, light, and thin crust that Korean fried chicken is famous for. The first fry cooks the chicken, and the second fry, at a higher temperature, crisps up the exterior and drives out any residual moisture.
*   **Use Potato Starch:** While cornstarch works, potato starch creates a lighter, airier, and crispier crust that holds up better to the sauce. It's worth seeking out.
*   **Don't Overcrowd the Pot:** Frying in small batches ensures the oil temperature remains consistent, leading to evenly cooked and crispy chicken. Overcrowding drops the temperature, resulting in greasy, soggy chicken.
*   **Pat the Chicken Dry:** Moisture is the enemy of crispiness. Before marinating and battering, ensure your chicken pieces are as dry as possible.
*   **Warm Sauce, Hot Chicken:** Toss the hot, freshly fried chicken directly into the warm sauce. This allows the sauce to adhere perfectly without cooling down the chicken or making it soggy too quickly.
*   **Monitor Oil Temperature:** Invest in a good thermometer. Maintaining the correct oil temperature for both fries is crucial for food safety and the perfect texture.
*   **Adjust Spice and Sweetness:** The Yangnyeom sauce is highly customizable. Love more heat? Add extra gochugaru. Prefer it sweeter? Increase the honey or corn syrup.

## Serving Suggestions for Yangnyeom Chicken

Yangnyeom Korean Fried Chicken is a showstopper on its own, but it pairs wonderfully with traditional Korean sides.

*   **Pickled Radish (Chicken Mu):** This is the quintessential pairing. The tangy, refreshing radish cuts through the richness of the fried chicken beautifully.
*   **Steamed Rice:** A simple bowl of white rice is perfect for soaking up any extra sauce.
*   **Kimchi:** The fermented, spicy cabbage offers another layer of flavor and a probiotic boost.
*   **Coleslaw:** A creamy, cool coleslaw can provide a nice contrast to the sweet and spicy chicken.
*   **Beer (Chimaek):** In Korea, fried chicken and beer (Chimaek, a portmanteau of "chicken" and "maekju" meaning beer) is a beloved combination.
*   **Garnish:** A sprinkle of toasted sesame seeds and chopped green onions adds a lovely finish and fresh aroma.

## Variations and Substitutions for Yangnyeom Sauce

While the classic Yangnyeom Chicken sauce is divine, don't hesitate to experiment:

*   **Spice Level:** Easily adjust the amount of gochujang and gochugaru to suit your palate. For milder flavor, reduce the gochujang and omit gochugaru. For more heat, add more of both!
*   **Sweetness:** Use maple syrup, agave nectar, or even plain sugar if you don't have honey or corn syrup. Adjust to taste.
*   **Tanginess:** If you prefer a more pronounced tang, a splash of apple cider vinegar can be used in place of some rice vinegar, or increase the ketchup slightly.
*   **Garlic Lover's:** Feel free to double the amount of minced garlic in the sauce for an extra pungent kick.
*   **Soy Garlic Variation:** For a non-spicy alternative, you can create a "Ganjang" or Soy Garlic sauce. Reduce the gochujang significantly (or omit it entirely), increase the soy sauce, add extra garlic, and a touch more honey/sugar. This creates a savory, sweet, and garlicky glaze.
*   **Gluten-Free:** Use tamari instead of soy sauce and ensure your potato starch is pure (most are naturally GF).
*   **Vegan:** For a plant-based version, use a vegan chicken substitute (like fried cauliflower or plant-based nuggets) and ensure your gochujang is vegan (most are, but check ingredients).

Making Yangnyeom Korean Fried Chicken at home is a rewarding culinary adventure. With a little patience and these detailed instructions, you’ll be able to create a dish that rivals your favorite Korean restaurant. Get ready to impress your family and friends with this incredibly flavorful and crispy Korean Chicken Recipe – a true taste sensation!
